name: X25
description: X.25 (ITU-T X.25 packet switching) and IP over public data networks

rfc1031.title: MILNET name domain transition
rfc1031.abstract: This RFC consolidates information necessary for the implementation of domain style names throughout the DDN/MILNET Internet community.  The introduction of domain style names will impact all hosts in the DDN/MILNET Internet.  This RFC is designed as an aid to implementors and administrators by providing: 1) an overview of the transition process from host tables to domains, 2) a timetable for the transition, and 3) references to documentation and software relating to the domain system.

rfc1044.title: Internet Protocol on Network System's HYPERchannel: Protocol Specification
rfc1044.abstract: This memo intends to provide a complete discussion of the protocols and techniques used to embed DoD standard Internet Protocol datagrams (and its associated higher level protocols) on Network Systems Corporation's HYPERchannel equipment.  This document is directed toward network planners and implementors who are already familiar with the TCP/IP protocol suite and the techniques used to carry TCP/IP traffic on common networks such as the DDN or the Ethernet.  No great familiarity with NSC products is assumed; an appendix is devoted to a review of NSC technologies and protocols.

rfc1086.title: ISO-TP0 bridge between TCP and X.25
rfc1086.abstract: This memo proposes a standard for the Internet community.  Hosts on the Internet that choose to implement ISO TP0 transport connectivity between TCP and X.25 based hosts are expected to experiment with this proposal.  TCP port 146 is reserved for this proposal.

rfc1090.title: SMTP on X.25
rfc1090.abstract: This memo proposes a standard for SMTP on the virtual circuit facility provided by the X.25 standard of the CCITT.

rfc1133.title: Routing between the NSFNET and the DDN
rfc1133.abstract: This document is a case study of the implementation of routing between the NSFNET and the DDN components (the MILNET and the ARPANET).  We hope that it can be used to expand towards interconnection of other Administrative Domains.  We would welcome discussion and suggestions about the methods employed for the interconnections.  No standards are specified in this memo.

rfc1236.title: IP to X.121 address mapping for DDN
rfc1236.abstract: This memo defines a standard way of converting IP addresses to CCITT X.121 addresses and is the recommended standard for use on the Internet, specifically for the Defense Data Network (DDN).  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  It does not specify an Internet standard.

rfc1293.title: Inverse Address Resolution Protocol

group.name: IP Over Large Public Data Networks

rfc1293.abstract: This memo describes additions to ARP that will allow a station to request a protocol address corresponding to a given hardware address. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc1294.title: Multiprotocol Interconnect over Frame Relay

group.name: IP Over Large Public Data Networks

rfc1294.abstract: This memo describes an encapsulation method for carrying network interconnect traffic over a Frame Relay backbone.  It covers aspects of both Bridging and Routing. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc1315.title: Management Information Base for Frame Relay DTEs

group.name: IP Over Large Public Data Networks

rfc1315.abstract: This memo defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for use with network management protocols in TCP/IP-based internets.  In particular, it defines objects for managing Frame Relay. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc1356.title: Multiprotocol Interconnect on X.25 and ISDN in the Packet Mode

group.name: IP Over Large Public Data Networks

rfc1356.abstract: This document specifies the encapsulation of IP and other network layer protocols over X.25 networks, in accordance and alignment with ISO/IEC and CCITT standards.  It is a replacement for RFC 877, "A Standard for the Transmission of IP Datagrams Over Public Data Networks" [1]. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc1362.title: Novell IPX over Various WAN Media (IPXWAN)
rfc1362.abstract: This document describes how Novell IPX operates over various WAN media.  Specifically, it describes the common "IPX WAN" protocol Novell uses to exchange necessary router to router information prior to exchanging standard IPX routing information and traffic over WAN datalinks.  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  It does not specify an Internet standard.

rfc1381.title: SNMP MIB Extension for X.25 LAPB
rfc1381.abstract: This memo defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for use with network management protocols in TCP/IP-based internets.  In particular, it defines objects for managing the Link Layer of X.25, LAPB. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc1382.title: SNMP MIB Extension for the X.25 Packet Layer
rfc1382.abstract: This memo defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for use with network management protocols in TCP/IP-based internets. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc1433.title: Directed ARP

group.name: IP Over Large Public Data Networks

rfc1433.abstract: Directed ARP is a dynamic address resolution procedure that enables hosts and routers to resolve advertised potential next-hop IP addresses on foreign IP networks to their associated link level addresses.  This memo defines an Experimental Protocol for the Internet community.

rfc1461.title: SNMP MIB extension for Multiprotocol Interconnect over X.25
rfc1461.abstract: This memo defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for use with network management protocols in TCP/IP-based internets.  In particular, it defines objects for managing Multiprotocol Interconnect (including IP) traffic carried over X.25. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc1490.title: Multiprotocol Interconnect over Frame Relay

group.name: IP Over Large Public Data Networks

rfc1490.abstract: This memo describes an encapsulation method for carrying network interconnect traffic over a Frame Relay backbone.  It covers aspects of both Bridging and Routing.  Additionally, it describes a simple fragmentation procedure for carrying large frames over a frame relay network with a smaller MTU. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc1598.title: PPP in X.25
rfc1598.abstract: The Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) provides a standard method for transporting multi-protocol datagrams over point-to-point links.  This document describes the use of X.25 for framing PPP encapsulated packets. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc1613.title: cisco Systems X.25 over TCP (XOT)
rfc1613.abstract: This memo documents a method of sending X.25 packets over IP internets by encapsulating the X.25 Packet Level in TCP packets.  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  This memo does not specify an Internet standard of any kind.

rfc874.title: Critique of X.25
rfc874.abstract: This RFC is an analysis of X.25 pointing out some problems in the conceptual model, particularly the conflict between the interface aspects and the end-to-end aspects.  The memo also touches on security, and implementation issues.  Originally published as M82-50 by the MITRE Corporation, Bedford, Massachusetts.
